messages:
maya: heads-up — after the driver upgrade to NVIDIA 545.1 on the H100 pool (~us-west-2), we're seeing TensorRT engine creation failures and xFormers kernel rejects. Symptoms started ~20m after the rollout. :warning:

deploy-bot: canary deploy (node-group: h100-canary-usw2) reported 7/12 failed health checks, rolling back to previous driver on that group. logs attached to the canary run. :gear:

samir: can you paste the exact error from the TRT log and dmesg? also which model/container was hitting it?

maya: snippet from pod logs and dmesg:
```
[TRT] ERROR: Engine creation failed: cudaErrorLaunchFailure during init kernels
[TRT] ERROR: Plugin registration failed: PTX kernel rejected: ptxVersion 8.8 vs device 9.x
nvrm: GPU 0: ptx checksum mismatch, rejecting module
```
Model: chat-embedder-v2 (fp16, cached kv), container image: inference:v3.12, uses xformers flash attention and TRT engine caching.

olga: looks like PTX compatibility break — new driver enforces stricter PTX checks on generated kernels from FlashAttention/xformers and some TRT cached engines. Could be new NVRTC/toolchain produced ptx incompatible with H100 SM version.

ben: confirm if this is only on H100 or also on A100? PTX mismatch suggests we need to recompile kernels with nvcc targeting sm_90 or regenerate TRT engines. If it's widespread, rolling back driver is fastest.

maya: A100 nodes not affected in our sample; only H100 pools with the 545 driver. Canary nodes show the worst failures; prod has ~12% H100 instances on that driver so some fraction of traffic hit failing nodes -> increased latency and queued requests.

samir: can we trigger a safe fallback: TTL-based routing to older pool? Also temporary autoscaler bump to shift work off H100s until rollback/patch?

olga: we can add a routing rule to prefer a100/dedicated pools for chat-embedder-v2 for next 30m. I'll open a quick console change. Also recommend disabling TRT engine cache warmup for that model so it won't attempt to load incompatible engines.

ben: short-term workaround: set ENV VARS in pods: TRT_DISABLE_CACHE=1 and XFORMERS_USE_FUSED_ATTENTION=0 to force reference kernels. That will increase token cost/latency but avoids ptx load failures.

canary-bot: rollback to driver 543.0 initiated on h100-canary-usw2 at 1968054380. Rolling back 12 nodes. ETA ~8m.

lorna: cost/time impact: if we route to A100 or fall back to non-fused kernels, token cost rises ~25% and latency +30-50ms per request. If rollback takes >15m we should notify customers on ops-status.

maya: opened internal incident INC-4921 and attached diagnostic bundle: /links/internal/incidents/INC-4921. I also uploaded core dumps and nvlog tar.

samir: action list: 1) Pause H100 driver rollout in other regions. 2) Fleet-wide canary checks for PTX rejection signature. 3) Rebuild TRT caches with updated toolchain (if driver stays). 4) Update runbooks to include TRT_DISABLE_CACHE and xformers flags as emergency knobs.

olga: I'll coordinate rebuild of TRT engines on the model infra side; but that might take hours per model. We need a plan if driver stays (recompile pipeline with nvcc targeting sm_90 and reserialize TRT engines).

ben: also watch for libnccl ABI mismatches in case we see hangs — PTX rejects may be the first signal but NCCL/libcuda mismatches cause different failure modes. Check `nvidia-smi` driver version and `ldd` on libnvinfer so we know what's shipped with containers.

maya: update: rollback completed on canary at 1968054475, canary healthy. Starting staggered rollback for 60% of nodes in the affected hostpool; holding 40% to monitor.

lorna: please track minutes and added cost impact to INC-4921. Notifying sales for any customers experiencing increased 503s.

samir: good postmortem items: better canary signal for PTX/engine load, include a quick smoke that loads common TRT engine shapes and calls `IPluginV2::initialize()` during canary.

maya: thanks all. I'll post a summary to #incidents and ping infra-leads. If rollback completes and stability confirmed, we'll gate the 545 driver rollout until we rebuild engine cache and validate xformers kernels. :white_check_mark:
